newsitem.title: INDIA: India party chief accused in journalists row.
newsitem.headline: India party chief accused in journalists row.

text.p: Police said on Saturday that they would investigate allegations against the president of India's Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) that he assaulted journalists who were staking out his house.

A police official told Reuters that Kanshi Ram, a key ally of former Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao's Congress party, faced complaints of rioting and causing minor injuries to journalists on Friday.
Newspapers in the Indian capital splashed front-page pictures of Ram slapping a reporter.
Journalists said Ram led an unprovoked attack and slapped a television reporter.
"We all went to the police station. We have all filed a statement," said Maya Mirchandani, a reporter for New Delhi Television.
She said she was pushed but some others were attacked by Ram or his aides.
Journalists said they were keeping a vigil outside his home in a public road and tried to get access through his secretarial staff who sit in a front office near the gate.
An aide at Ram's residence said the leader had no comment.
Ram has been the object of a vigil by television crews since the end of elections in Uttar Pradesh, India's most populous and politically crucial state earlier this month.
Police said they would investigate and would charge Ram if the journalists' evidence is found to be true. If not, they can cancel the complaint against Ram only before a court of law.
